bib.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents

question: Can generating a CLIP image embedding from a caption (prior) and then decoding it with a diffusion model improve text-to-image diversity without losing photorealism or caption similarity?
hypothesis: Explicitly generating CLIP image representations improves image diversity with minimal loss in photorealism and caption similarity (abstract).
contributions: Two-stage unCLIP: prior generating a CLIP image embedding from a caption plus a diffusion decoder inverting the CLIP image encoder
Diffusion prior in latent space matching or beating an autoregressive prior at lower compute
Language-guided zero-shot image manipulations (variations, interpolations, text diffs) via the bipartite latent (z_i, x_T)

method.summary: unCLIP stacks a prior P(z_i|y) (AR or diffusion) that maps a caption to a CLIP image embedding with a GLIDE-style diffusion decoder P(x|z_i,y) at 64x64, then two diffusion upsamplers to 256 and 1024. CLIP is frozen while the prior and decoder train. Compared to GLIDE by human evaluation, FID on MS-COCO and an aesthetic probe.

datasets.name: CLIP dataset + DALL-E dataset (CLIP encoder training)
datasets.split: sampled with equal probability from the two datasets

datasets.name: DALL-E dataset (decoder, upsamplers, prior)
datasets.preprocessing: noisier CLIP dataset excluded from generative stack because it hurt sample quality

datasets.name: MS-COCO validation
datasets.split: validation set, zero-shot (not trained on COCO train); 256x256 FID; 1,000 captions for diversity grids

datasets.name: AVA
datasets.split: images and mean ratings for aesthetic linear probe

datasets.name: GPT-3 generated artistic captions
datasets.source: GPT-3 prompted with captions of existing artwork (real and AI generated)

models.name: unCLIP decoder
models.architecture: GLIDE diffusion model with CLIP embedding projected and added to timestep embedding plus 4 extra context tokens

other.guidance: CLIP embedding zeroed 10% and caption dropped 50% in training; Section 5.1 says CLIP image embedding dropped 5% of the time

models.name: AR prior
models.architecture: Transformer text encoder (width 2048, 24 blocks, 32 heads, context 256) and causal decoder (width 1664, 24 blocks, 26 heads, context 384); CLIP embedding PCA to 319 of 1,024 dims, each quantised into 1,024 buckets

other.conditioning: caption, CLIP text embedding, quantised z_i.z_t token (sampled from top half of distribution; percentiles 50%, 70%, 85%, 95% swept, 50 best)

models.name: Diffusion prior
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer with causal mask, width 2048, 24 blocks, 32 heads, text context 256; predicts unnoised z_i directly with MSE

other.sampling: Analytic DPM, 64 strided steps; 1000 diffusion steps; cosine schedule
other.sample selection: 2 samples of z_i, keep higher dot product with z_t

models.name: CLIP (paper's own)
models.architecture: ViT-H/16 image encoder at 256x256, width 1280, 32 blocks; text Transformer width 1024, 24 blocks, causal mask

other.training: lr 3e-4, SAM rho 0.1, per-replica batch 64, rest as Radford et al. 2021

training.objective: Prior: MSE on predicted unnoised z_i, L = E ||f(z_i^(t), t, y) - z_i||^2 (diffusion prior); autoregressive likelihood over quantised PCA codes (AR prior); standard diffusion loss for decoder with learned sigma
training.optimizer: Adam with corrected (decoupled) weight decay, beta1 0.9; beta2 0.91 (AR prior), 0.96 (diffusion prior), 0.999 (decoder, upsamplers)
training.regularisation: EMA decay 0.999 (AR prior), 0.9999 (all others); Adam epsilon 1.0e-10, 1.0e-6, 1.0e-8; random crops at one-fourth target size for upsamplers

other.production model: a larger-data, longer-trained production version exists; its hyperparameters are not reported

inference.decoding: prior sample then decoder diffusion (250 strided steps) then DDIM upsamplers (27 and 15 steps)
inference.samples: four images per prompt for aesthetic eval (2048 images over 512 prompts); 4x4 sample grids for diversity eval; 2 prior samples per caption for diffusion prior

parameters.prior guidance: guiding prior hurt aesthetic results; only decoder guided in that eval

other.hyperparameter sweeps: sampling hyperparameters swept per model using a CLIP linear probe proxy for photorealism, fixed across three human evaluations

metrics.name: Human preference (photorealism, caption similarity, diversity)
metrics.definition: probability unCLIP beats GLIDE in pairwise (or grid-pair) comparison with a 'Not sure' option; 95% normal-approximation CI

metrics.name: Mean AVA prediction
metrics.definition: CLIP linear regression on AVA mean ratings, averaged over images

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: computed with respect to the training dataset

eval.protocol: Human evaluations n = 1,000 comparisons with 95% normal-approximation intervals; diversity uses 1,000 MS-COCO validation captions. Evaluator count and payment not stated.

availability.data: DALL-E and CLIP datasets are not released in the paper

evidence.quote: randomly setting the CLIP embeddings to zero (or a learned embedding) 10% of the time, and randomly dropping the text caption 50% of the time
evidence.where: Section 2.1; Section 5.1 says the CLIP image embedding is dropped 5% of the time

results.claim: unCLIP with diffusion prior sets the best zero-shot MS-COCO FID among compared zero-shot models
results.setup: MS-COCO val 256x256, zero-shot, decoder guidance 1.25, diffusion prior
results.quote: We ﬁnd that, compared to these other zero-shot models, unCLIP achieves a new state-of-the-art FID of 10.39 when sampling with the diffusion prior.

results.claim: Humans prefer GLIDE slightly for photorealism over unCLIP (diffusion prior)
results.setup: Pairwise human eval, n=1000, sampling hyperparameters swept with proxy

results.claim: unCLIP diffusion prior is strongly preferred over GLIDE for diversity
results.setup: Two 4x4 grids per caption, 1,000 MS-COCO val captions

results.claim: unCLIP diffusion prior loses to GLIDE on caption similarity
results.table: Table 1, row Diffusion, column Caption Similarity

results.claim: AR prior win rates vs GLIDE are lower than diffusion prior
Feeding the unCLIP decoder a prior-generated image embedding beats using a text embedding or caption only on FID
results.setup: small models: small unCLIP stack (diffusion prior + decoder) FID 7.99
results.note: Order is inferred: 'text-embedding decoder, unCLIP stack, text embeddings fed zero-shot to the unCLIP decoder' per preceding sentence, so 9.16 is text-embedding decoder, 7.99 is unCLIP stack, 16.55 is zero-shot text embedding.
results.quote: We ﬁnd that these approaches respectively score FIDs of 9.16, 7.99, and 16.55 on a test set

results.claim: Humans prefer full unCLIP stack over text-embedding decoder for photorealism
results.quote: We ﬁnd that humans prefer the full unCLIP stack 57.0% ± 3.1% of the time for photorealism and 53.1% ± 3.1% of the time for caption similarity.

results.claim: GLIDE at guidance scale 2.0 is close to unCLIP in photorealism and caption similarity but less diverse
results.setup: human eval across GLIDE guidance scales (Fig 10)
results.quote: We ﬁnd that GLIDE at guidance scale 2.0 is very close to the photorealism and caption similarity of unCLIP, while still producing less diverse samples.

results.claim: Diffusion prior outperforms AR prior at comparable size with less training compute
PCA keeps 319 of 1,024 CLIP dimensions with under 1% mean-squared reconstruction error, cutting AR tokens threefold
results.setup: CLIP image embeddings, CLIP trained with SAM
results.quote: We are able to preserve nearly all of the information2 by retaining only 319 principal components out of the original 1,024.

results.claim: Training dataset for decoder, upsamplers and prior
results.quote: When training the decoder, upsamplers, and prior, we use only the DALL-E dataset [40] (approximately 250M images).

results.claim: unCLIP binds attributes to objects worse than GLIDE and struggles to render coherent text
Guiding unCLIP raises aesthetic score without lowering recall; guiding the prior hurts
results.setup: 512 GPT-3 artistic prompts, 4 images each, 2048 images; AVA linear probe

limits: Worse than GLIDE at binding attributes to objects (Fig 14, 15) and at producing coherent text (Fig 16), hypothesised to follow from CLIP embedding and BPE
Weak detail in complex scenes, blamed on 64x64 base resolution (Fig 17)
Humans still slightly prefer GLIDE for photorealism and caption similarity
Hardware, compute, wall-clock, seeds, LR schedule and warmup not stated; datasets not released
Production model differs (more data filtered for aesthetics/safety, inpainting) and its hyperparameters are not given
Raises risk profile over GLIDE; bias behaviour of the architecture needs more research
Human-evaluation sweeps use a proxy probe trained on earlier human comparisons

(z_i, x_T): CLIP image embedding plus DDIM-inverted residual latent
normalised difference of CLIP text embeddings used to rotate an image embedding via slerp
